meta.title: SNAP, food banks and hunger, 18 days of posts
meta.subject: food security policy in Texas — SNAP eligibility, work requirements and federal cost shifts, HHSC's SNAP administration and error rates, Summer EBT and school meal programs, food banks and the Houston Food Bank, the Department of Agriculture's nutrition programs, and hunger as a political issue
meta.subtitle: Oct 1 to Oct 18, 2026. Each dot is one post with 1K+ views about Texas SNAP, food banks and hunger, plus every post repeating an earlier one, in the lane for what it argues. Higher and bigger means more views. White means 90% or more the same words as an earlier post, with a white line back to it. Coloured lines link a post to the post it quoted or replied to. Updated daily.

lanes.label: Food bank drives and partnerships
lanes.description: Posts promote community, sports and civic fundraisers and food drives for Texas food banks as the local, charitable answer to hunger.

lanes.label: SNAP fraud and noncitizen benefits
lanes.description: Posts claim SNAP and EBT money is lost to fraud, trafficking, or payments to non-citizens, and use it to argue that taxpayers are being fleeced.

lanes.label: Strapped families flood food banks
lanes.description: Posts argue that rising need is pushing struggling Texas families to the Houston Food Bank and similar groups because other help is out of reach.

lanes.label: Kids losing school and summer meals
lanes.description: Posts say Republicans are starving poor children by ending summer meal programs, cutting free school meals and shrinking children's benefits.

lanes.label: GOP cuts and paperwork burden
lanes.description: Posts blame Republicans in Washington and Austin for cutting benefits, adding paperwork and work requirements, and shifting costs onto Texans.

lanes.label: School meals culture-war claims
lanes.description: Posts frame Texas school meal policy as a culture-war fight, for example claims that halal or Sharia-linked rules are being pushed into school lunches.

lanes.label: Pushback
lanes.description: Posts doubting, mocking, fact-checking or arguing against the dominant framings.
